import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify highly associated features using Welch t-test
    t_stats = [stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)], 
                              feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)])[0] 
               for fid in feats.ids]
    
    # Select top features by absolute t-statistic
    top_indices = np.argsort(np.abs(t_stats))[::-1][:20]
    top_features = [feats.ids[i] for i in top_indices]
    
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in top_features]].T)
    to_remove = set()
    for i in range(len(top_features)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_features)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) > 0.6:
                to_remove.add(top_features[j])
    
    unique_features = [fid for fid in top_features if fid not in to_remove]
    
    # If no mechanism, return empty design
    if len(unique_features) < 2:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Cluster features into modules
    X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in unique_features]]
    clustering = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=1, linkage='ward')
    cluster_labels = clustering.fit_predict(X)
    
    # Select best module (most significant features)
    module_features = unique_features
    
    # Create weighted score from module features
    weights = np.array([abs(t_stats[feats.column(fid)]) for fid in module_features])
    weights = weights / np.sum(weights)  # Normalize
    
    # Return design with module features
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(module_features[:MAX_DRIVERS]),
        columns=tuple(module_features),
        products=(),
        loadings=dict(zip(module_features, weights))
    )
